angle_types.label: Pain-based
angle_types.description: Name the real discomfort, worry, or guilt directly — the thing the owner is actually feeling — then let Vitality sit alongside it as relief, not a cure.

angle_types.label: Desire-based
angle_types.description: Paint the aspirational outcome or identity the owner wants for their dog. Inspirational, forward-looking, not fear-driven.

angle_types.label: Problem / Solution
angle_types.description: State the problem plainly, then the solution just as plainly. No embellishment, no emotional framing — just clear cause and effect.

angle_types.label: Social proof
angle_types.description: Lean on 'other owners like you already do this.' Community validation and shared experience, not hype or manufactured urgency.

angle_types.label: Curiosity / Pattern interrupt
angle_types.description: Open with a genuinely surprising or counterintuitive observation from the comments that makes an owner want to know more — without becoming clickbait or breaking Dogist's trust.

angle_types.label: Niche-specific
angle_types.description: Speak to one narrow, specific situation or owner identity so precisely that it feels made for exactly that person, not a general dog-owner audience.

themes.label: Picky Eaters Rejecting Foods
themes.problem_statement: Dogs are selective eaters who refuse many foods, treats, flavors, and textures, making consistent feeding and nutrition difficult for owners.
themes.want_statement: Owners want their dogs to accept a wider variety of foods and treats, including unfamiliar options, without being so selective.

angles.dogist_style_angle: You made the homemade biscuits. You tried the blueberry treats. You watched them sniff, walk away, and look at you like you personally offended them. Feeding a picky dog isn't a nutrition problem — it's a daily morale problem. Vitality Chews are salmon-flavored, not because we gave up on blueberries, but because your dog shouldn't have to either. The antioxidants are still in there. The rejection, hopefully, isn't.
angles.why_this_type_fits: The frustration of a dog refusing food you prepared or purchased is the exact emotional wound this theme surfaces, and pain-based copy earns trust by naming it before offering anything.
